domain: International trade law / WTO dispute settlement: litigation escalation of formal trade disputes
prediction_question: At the instant a WTO member's Request for Consultations is circulated with a DS number - the moment a formal dispute enters the WTO dispute settlement system - will that dispute escalate to first-instance litigation (the Dispute Settlement Body establishes a panel for that DS number within the eligibility window), or will it end without one (settled in consultations, withdrawn, or lapsed)? The prospective user is a trade ministry or mission to the WTO in Geneva weighing litigation cost and coalition formation at filing time, and the research question the bench cares about: do the agreements cited, the measure/subject, and the pair's dispute history carry signal beyond complainant-respondent identity? The identity-prior risk is real (the afdb/wb-loan family defect) and is exactly what the pre-registered triad tests.
prediction_time: The circulation date of the Request for Consultations for the DS number (all WTO dates are Geneva-local circulation dates, published the same day to all members). Features available at that instant: complainant(s), respondent(s), the WTO agreements and provisions cited (the request itself cites them and is circulated at the instant), the measure/subject short title, the calendar, and trailing strictly-prior dispute history for the complainant-respondent pair. Every later stage (request for panel establishment, DSB establishment, panel composition, report, adoption) is outcome-side and excluded from features.
target_definition: Binary: the DSB establishes a panel for this DS number within the eligibility window (consultations request at least 24 months before the artifact cutoff - measured: 97.1% of establishments occur within 24 months of consultations, median 155 days, n=273). Label source columns (all post-instant stage dates) are excluded from every shipped CSV. No external threshold is involved (the event is the publisher's own procedural milestone), so the known-event requirement is met by named disputes with their published outcomes: DS600 Malaysia v EU palm oil (consultations 15 Jan 2021, panel established 28 May 2021) and DS620/DS631 (2023/2024 filings, no establishment yet - the censoring behaviour working as expected). Right-censoring: consultations inside the 24-month eligibility tail are excluded and counted, never labelled negative. Settlements are mostly NOT formally notified (the dates file carries one MAS date; the stage file counts 156 'mutually agreed solutions, lapse of authority' events across the whole era), so the negative class means 'no panel established by cutoff', a documented meaning, not 'settled'.

split_strategy: Population: every DS-numbered request for consultations 1995-present (the publisher's own counting convention per the stats page technical note; joint multi-member requests may share a document across DS numbers - one row per DS number). MEASURED windows from the publisher's own dates file (543 rows / 542 distinct DS / 5 Textiles Monitoring Body rows excluded and counted): train consultations 1995-2008 = 383 rows / 169 positives (44.1%); eval 2009-2014 = 100 / 67 (67.0%); holdout 2015-2018 = 55 / 37 (67.3%). Both classes present in every window; distinct positive complainant-respondent pairs 89 / 48 / 28. CONSTRUCTION OPTION, measured on the stage file only (2019-2025: 20/11, 5/7, 9/10, 8/1, 6/5, 10/4, 10/4 consultations/establishments): extend the holdout to 2019-2021 by extracting the modern tail from case pages (the dates file ends at DS543); the era shift in the base rate (44% -> 67% after 2009) is a real property of the system to declare, not to tune away. Eligibility cutoff: consultations >= 24 months before the artifact cutoff (97.1% of establishments within 24 months, median 155 days, p90 387 days, n=273). Label = DSB panel establishment for the DS within the eligibility window.

No bulk download channel exists for the per-DS features (the Data Portal resources are search apps), so the build enumerates ds<N>_e.htm pages; the numbers are extrapolated from the measured sample, stated as such.
measurements.licence_note_2026_11_06: Class A on two instruments: the dataset-level CC BY 4.0 license_id on both data.wto.org dispute packages, and the site copyright page's 'free for public use' grant for unrestricted official documents. Residual caveats recorded: (a) the Data Portal is marked BETA and the package records were created 2026-10-12 - a young instrument, but it is the publisher's own and dataset-specific; (b) the site-wide page restricts 'other material' (official publications) to non-commercial use with attribution - the shipped artifact redistributes no WTO prose, only structured facts from unrestricted official documents and the CC-BY database; (c) no-logo clause carries to LICENSE.md.

review: All five discovery contracts reconciled against recorded evidence (2026-11-06, discovery-only session; no construction, no score). (1) Redistribution SUPPORTED - class A: CC BY 4.0 dataset-level licence on both data.wto.org dispute packages (CKAN license_id measured via the API) plus the 'unrestricted official WTO documents and legal texts are free for public use' grant; caveats (BETA portal, non-commercial clause for publications, no-logo) recorded in measurements.licence_note_2026_11_06. (2) Prediction timing SUPPORTED - the instant is the circulation date of the DS-numbered request for consultations; every feature is documented by the publisher on the case page and in the request itself (agreements cited at filing); all later stage dates are outcome-side and excludable. Vintage: current-snapshot archive with a MEASURED coverage hole (the dates file ends DS543/2018; case pages carry 2019-2025) - the task is declared retrospective research with a current-vintage assumption (cpcb/afdb precedent); no operational as-of claim is made. (3) Target SUPPORTED - DSB panel establishment is the publisher's own procedural milestone, fully recorded per DS; censoring handled by a measured 24-month eligibility cutoff (97.1% resolution); 'no panel' is documented to mean not-established-by-cutoff, not settled (settlement notification is mostly absent - measured). (4) Split capacity SUPPORTED, measured from the publisher's own artifact: train 383/169, eval 100/67, holdout 55/37, both classes in every window, distinct positive pairs 89/48/28 (>20 minimum), plus a measured modern-tail extension option. (5) Not-a-mirror SUPPORTED - no ML-ready, split, scored task exists: prior art is econometric/game-theoretic escalation studies (Bernauer et al. 506-dyad selection models; KU Leuven SBI panel-phase model; Maggi & Staiger) and the Horn & Mavroidis legal-coding research dataset (507 disputes to 2016, 1,272 variables, 'only to be used for research purposes, and not for commercial purposes', World Bank/EUI mirrors) - a stale, research-terms coding dataset, not a benchmark; novelty verdict recorded via scripts/check-novelty.py. KNOWN RISK carried into construction: the label may be identity-dominated (complainant-respondent pair + era), the afdb/wb-loan family defect; the pre-registered triad must therefore include trailing pair/pair-year escalation rates and era priors as references to beat, with pair-clustered bootstrap intervals, and the deciding rule follows the standing order (headroom only if the model beats EVERY reference with a CI excluding zero; reference dominance -> drop).
next_action: Hand to construction (worker; discovery is complete and nothing was constructed or scored this session). (1) Enumerate the population: DS1..DS~641 via cases_e/ds<N>_e.htm (handle unused numbers as gaps, verify total against the stage-file 631/1995-2024 + current-year cross-checks, pin file digests and a vintage timestamp; the dates xlsx is a convenience anchor for DS1-543 ONLY - its tail is stale). (2) Extract per-DS at-instant features (complainant(s), respondent(s), agreements + provision families cited, measure/subject, consultations date) and lifecycle dates from the case pages; exclude all post-instant columns from shipped CSVs; count and exclude the TMB rows; repair-rule the 3 known malformed dates. (3) Build splits per split_strategy (one re-cut allowed before any score if a window bound fails the gate, reason recorded); label = panel establishment within the eligibility window; count the censored tail. (4) Pre-register the triad BEFORE any score: trailing complainant-respondent-pair escalation rate, trailing complainant rate, era/calendar prior, global rate; pair-clustered paired bootstrap; the afdb identity-prior precedent is the failure mode the triad exists to catch. (5) Then the standing ladder: full-artifact gate 1.5 with evaluation_contract (retrospective_research, isolated_rows, current-vintage assumption declared, prediction_time selection), exact-byte --accept, triad, full-model baseline job, pre-registered deciding rule (headroom only if EVERY reference is beaten with a CI excluding zero; reference dominance -> record the defect and DROP; inconclusive -> hold). Holdout never opened in dev.

prior_art: Horn & Mavroidis, The WTO Dispute Settlement Data Set 1995-2015 v4.0 (2016, World Bank-funded; EUI 2020 update); Bernauer et al., Dispute-Escalation in the WTO (ETH ISN WP 2006, 506 dyads); Maggi & Staiger (2015); Dresvyannikova (UTwente MA 2016, 159 cases)
novelty_check.theirs: The WTO publishes the case register itself (DS Database, per-DS gateway pages, stage-count xlsx, One-Page Case Summaries) and its Data Portal now labels both dispute datasets CC BY 4.0 - the raw data is theirs and stays theirs; the academic layer is econometric/game-theoretic escalation modeling (Bernauer et al. selection models on 506 dyads 1995-2003; Maggi & Staiger 388 disputes; KU Leuven statistical-backwards-induction panel-phase model; an MA thesis predicting panel requests on 159 cases) and case-level legal-coding research datasets: Horn & Mavroidis WTO DS Data Set v4.0 (507 disputes 1995-2016, 1,272 variables, research-only/no-commercial terms; EUI hosts a 2020 update; World Bank Data Catalog mirrors the 2006-era 351-dispute version) - none is an ML-ready prediction task with splits and a scored contract, and the coding datasets carry terms that forbid redistribution for our use
novelty_check.ours: Full-population at-filing escalation task on all DS-numbered WTO consultations requests 1995-present (641 through 2025): at the circulation instant of the request for consultations, predict whether the DSB establishes a panel for that DS, with temporal splits, a 24-month eligibility cutoff measured from the publisher's own artifact, pre-registered identity-prior references (trailing complainant-respondent-pair escalation rate, era priors) and a pair-clustered scored contract, built from the WTO's own CC BY 4.0 channels (data.wto.org dispute packages + per-DS gateway pages + stage-count aggregates), current through 2025
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
